briefFidelity: FAIL, on three counts, and I can prove I was not anchored because I wrote the contradicting words before opening the brief. (1) FORM. The brief asks for 'rounded forms, clustered and overlapping'. Unprompted I wrote that the work is built from 'exactly one primitive: the square... drawn flat, hard-edged' and that 'there is no line work, no curve'. Every tile confirms it - 1310661 is a hard heptagonal slab, 1475115 a spiked star of straight-edged quads, 1991107 a field of tilted squares. Not one rounded form exists anywhere in the twelve. (2) FEELING. The brief asks for 'biological rather than geometric... accretion, not design', and explicitly anticipates the risk by saying the regular construction must still feel organic. Before reading it I independently called these 'a mandala, a snowflake, a compass rose, a cut-paper doily' and 'a ceremonial object and its debris'. 1243682, 1835793 and 1203347 are exact rotational stamps about a single origin; nothing buds from anything, there are no generations, there is one stamp. That is design, and it is the pole the brief named as wrong. (3) MARKET STORY, which the brief calls 'the whole market story'. See marketResponse - the claimed direction is inverted. What the brief DOES get: the palette is exactly the commissioned verdigris-and-bone-over-deep-ink, and tokens do differ in spread and packing. Two axes delivered, three failed, including both the brief flags as decisive.
composition: Genuinely good, and the strongest thing here. Every tile has a real focal hierarchy - a dense medallion at centre, a scatter field falling away from it, and enough tonal separation that the eye lands in the middle first. 1310661 and 1475115 are the best of them: a solid teal core, a cream collar, and grey squares thinning outward, which is a proper figure-ground read. The frame is used rather than decorated - squares are cut in half at the edge on nearly every tile (1203347, 1366079, 1991107) and the crop makes the scatter feel like part of a larger field continuing past the viewBox, which is deliberate and works. The one real criticism is that it is the SAME composition twelve times: all twelve are centred, all twelve are medallion-plus-surround, and nothing is ever placed off-axis. 1991107 is the only tile that varies the schema at all, by inverting to a cream mass with a dark keyhole.
collectionCoherence: Strong, arguably the work's best axis. Shared near-black ground, one shared four-colour palette, the square-only vocabulary, centred radial symmetry and the outer scatter ring appear in all twelve without exception. Laid out on the contact sheet, 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1366079, 1733538 and 1835793 are obviously siblings; the outliers 1446330 (almost empty) and 1991107 (almost solid) still read as the same hand because the primitive and the palette never move. Nobody would mistake this for a folder of unrelated images. If anything coherence is slightly over-served at the expense of seedVariation - the family resemblance in the middle six is close to identity.
palette: Chosen, and correct against the brief - the one axis where my blind description and the brief used the same vocabulary. I wrote 'muted sea-green / verdigris teal', 'bone/ivory cream' and 'near-black charcoal with a faint blue-green cast' before reading a word of the commission, which asked for verdigris and bone over deep ink, damp and mineral rather than bright. It is damp and mineral: nothing here is saturated or cheerful. The ground supports rather than competes - the near-black lets the cream carry maximum punch on 1310661 and 1475115, and the grey ladder gives the scatter depth without pulling attention off the centre. The failure mode is contrast collapse where translucent cream stacks on translucent cream: 1985692 loses its entire outer scatter into the pale mass, and 1366079 and 1991107 suffer the same to a lesser degree.
seedVariation: Real range, but nearly all of it on one axis - ink density - and that leaves the middle of the distribution repetitive. The extremes are unmistakably different works: 1446330 is an almost empty black field with a few grey squares, 1991107 is a near-solid cream slab with a dark keyhole, 1310661 is a bold teal disc, 1985692 a pale low-contrast bloom. But 1203347, 1283437, 1366079, 1733538 and 1835793 are the same picture at slightly different weights - cream rosette, teal inside, grey scatter around - and 1203347 versus 1733538 is close to one work at two rotations. The opposite failure does not occur; nothing here strays far enough to stop being one project. Density variation does satisfy the brief's 'how far the colony has spread and how densely it has packed', so this axis is a qualified pass on the brief's own terms even though the middle six under-deliver.
thumbnailSurvival: Mixed, and it separates the collection into three tiers. The centre-plus-scatter idea survives completely at 120px - every tile still reads as a medallion on black. The extremes read well and stay distinct small: 1310661 and 1475115 as bold teal discs, 1991107 as a pale slab with a hole, 1985692 as a pale bloom. The middle six do not: the interior filigree of 1203347, 1243682 and 1835793 turns to mush at 120 and those tiles are then separated only by overall lightness, leaving 1203347, 1283437 and 1733538 close to interchangeable at browse size. Two tiles fail outright. 1446330 at 120px reads as an empty tile - a viewer scrolling a gallery would take it for a broken render, not a quiet token. The teal chips on 1561509 and 1283437 shrink to specks that read as dust on the screen rather than as drawing. In the state sheet at 120 the stress row is obvious on all four seeds, but neutral versus recovery is genuinely hard to call on 1203347 and 1243682.
marketResponse: This is the decisive failure and it is not a near miss - it is backwards. The brief states 'recovery pushes the colony outward and multiplies its members, stress pulls it back toward the centre and reduces it'. The sheets do the reverse. STRESS EXPANDS. On 1310661 the teal stops being a contained core and floods almost the entire frame, leaving a small cream flower at centre - the colony does not retreat, it engulfs the tile. On 1203347 the cream ring cracks apart into detached blocks thrown WIDER around a black star-shaped void. On 1283437 a pale radial bloom opens outward and displaces the teal core. On 1243682 the fine filigree is replaced by a bigger, blunter six-point star; member count drops but extent grows, so even the one seed that partly reduces does so while spreading, not while pulling back to centre. RECOVERY DOES NOTHING. On all four seeds it is a near-return to neutral: at 256px I can find differences (1203347 recovery carries more teal chips out in the ring, 1310661 recovery has a heavier cream collar) but nothing pushes outward and nothing multiplies. At 120px, recovery versus neutral on 1203347 and 1243682 is a coin flip. So the brief's growth pole is invisible and its retreat pole is rendered as violent expansion. The brief's one procedural requirement - 'plainly visible at thumbnail size' - is technically met, but it is the wrong change made visible, which is worse than an invisible one: a holder watching drawdown would see the colony bloom.
tokenIdentity: Holds on two of the four state seeds and breaks on two. 1203347 and 1243682 stay recognisably themselves across neutral, stress and recovery - same symmetry order, same colour proportion, same silhouette envelope, only the internal packing changes. 1310661 does not: neutral is a contained teal heptagon in a cream halo, stress is a frame-filling teal ground with a small cream flower on it, and figure and ground have swapped roles - at 120px those two tiles read as different objects by different rules, not as one token under pressure. 1283437 is a milder version of the same problem, with the stress bloom replacing the teal core so that the thing identifying the token at neutral is the thing removed at stress. Recovery preserves identity everywhere, but only because it barely changes anything.
artifacts: No true rendering defects - nothing is broken, clipped wrongly, or misplaced. Edge clipping is pervasive (1203347, 1366079, 1991107, and every tile in the state sheet) but is clearly intentional and reads as a field continuing past the crop rather than as a mistake. The real complaints are compositional. Contrast collapse where translucent cream stacks on cream swallows the outer scatter entirely on 1985692 and substantially on 1366079 and 1991107, so a whole layer of the vocabulary disappears. 1446330 is so sparse that at 120px it is indistinguishable from an empty tile, which will read to a viewer as a failure state. The small teal chips on 1561509 and 1283437 sit at a size where they look like sensor dust rather than deliberate marks. On 1310661 stress the flooded teal reaches all four edges and the grey squares sit on top of it as unrelated stickers, which reads as a background fill rather than as composition.
reasoning: This is competent, coherent, well-composed work with a genuinely correct palette, and it is not the thing that was commissioned. Two failures decide it, and both are gate failures rather than quality judgements. First, form and feeling: the brief asked for rounded, biological, accretive growth and explicitly warned that regular construction must not read as geometric design - before I had read a word of it I described hard-edged squares, no curves anywhere, and mandalas, snowflakes and cut-paper doilies. That is the brief's own failure example. Second, and worse, the market story the brief calls 'the whole market story' runs backwards: stress is supposed to pull the colony toward the centre and reduce it, and instead 1310661 floods the frame with teal, 1203347 throws its ring apart into a wider scatter, and 1283437 blooms outward; recovery is supposed to push outward and multiply, and instead it is a near-copy of neutral on all four seeds and a coin flip against it at 120px. An invisible transition would have been a failure to deliver; an inverted one that is plainly visible actively tells the holder the opposite of what the market did. I am refusing an accomplished object because it is not the answer to this brief, which is exactly what the gate is for, and I would refuse it again if the middle six seeds were sharper.
wouldChange: Three concrete things, in order. (1) Swap the primitive. The brief says rounded; ship rounded - discs, lozenges, or squares with a corner radius large enough to read as cellular at 120px. This alone moves the work from ceremonial geometry toward the commissioned biology, and it costs nothing structurally since the placement logic is unchanged. (2) Invert the state mapping, which appears to be simply wired the wrong way round: make the state that currently reads as 1310661-stress into RECOVERY (it already pushes outward and floods, which is the growth the brief wants), and author a genuine contraction for stress - fewer members, smaller radius, the colony pulled back toward centre against more visible ground. Then verify it on the 120px state sheet, because that is where 1203347 neutral and recovery are currently indistinguishable. (3) Break the single-origin rotational stamp. Offset each generation's centre slightly from its parent so members bud off one another instead of all rotating about one point; that is what would make 1243682 and 1835793 read as accretion rather than as a doily, and it would also pull the middle six seeds - 1203347, 1283437, 1366079, 1733538 - apart from each other at browse size, where they currently converge.
